title.ko: 부정어 도치: Not only · Never · Rarely · Hardly … when · No sooner … than
title.en: negative inversion: Not only, Never, Rarely, Hardly … when, No sooner … than

explain.ko: 부정어나 제한의 뜻을 가진 부사구가 문장 앞에 오면 주어와 조동사의 순서가 바뀝니다(도치). Never, Rarely, Seldom, Hardly … when, No sooner … than, Not only … but also, Under no circumstances, Only then, Only after … 등이 대표적입니다. 조동사가 없으면 do/does/did를 넣습니다(Not only did he apologise ...). No sooner와 Hardly 뒤에는 과거완료를 쓰며, 격식 있는 글과 연설에서 강조 효과를 냅니다.
explain.en: When a negative or restrictive adverbial opens a clause, the subject and auxiliary swap places. Common triggers are never, rarely, seldom, hardly … when, no sooner … than, not only … but also, under no circumstances, only then and only after. If there is no auxiliary, add do/does/did (Not only did he apologise ...). No sooner and hardly take the past perfect. The pattern adds emphasis in formal writing and speeches.

head: 도입어 / Opener

rows: Rarely do we see such talent.

notes.ko: 도치가 일어난 뒤의 어순은 의문문과 같습니다.
notes.en: After inversion the word order is the same as in a question.

notes.ko: No sooner는 than과, Hardly는 when과 함께 씁니다.
notes.en: No sooner pairs with than; hardly pairs with when.

notes.ko: 너무 자주 쓰면 부자연스러우니 강조하고 싶은 곳에만 쓰세요.
notes.en: Overuse sounds unnatural, so save it for real emphasis.

prompt.ko: 부정어 도치를 사용해 인상 깊었던 경험이나 놀라운 사건을 4문장으로 써 보세요.
prompt.en: Write 4 sentences about a striking experience or surprising event using negative inversion.

task.model: Never had I seen such a beautiful sunrise. No sooner had we reached the summit than the clouds began to clear. Not only was the view stunning, but the air was also remarkably clear. Only then did the hard climb feel rewarded.

model_trans.ko: 그렇게 아름다운 일출은 본 적이 없었어요. 정상에 도착하자마자 구름이 걷히기 시작했어요. 풍경이 아름다웠을 뿐만 아니라 공기도 아주 맑았어요. 그제서야 오르기 힘들었던 시간이 보상받는 느낌이었어요.
model_trans.en: Never had I seen such a beautiful sunrise. No sooner had we reached the summit than the clouds began to clear. Not only was the view stunning, but the air was also remarkably clear. Only then did the hard climb feel rewarded.
